Its compatibility path queues durable local approval requests and can render an allow after consume_native_review_approval for a narrowly reusable exact request. Non-command proof and command payload-bound reuse are distinct from the external Rust enrollment/claim/consume route.
findings.implication: Rust-owned cryptographic approval code does not prove every current delivered approval passed that route. Legacy compatibility reuse must not be counted as qualified native consume, nor expanded to mutable-code commands such as Ollama.
findings.required_resolution: Describe current compatibility and external native-approval routes separately, with actual binding/reuse/consume evidence and existing unresolved RSP080 scope. No allowlist expansion or approval authority change is authorized by this review.

resolved_source_positions.conclusion: Current native evaluation and final delivery are different results. Ordinary unavailable PreTool requests continue with warn/allow; the two designated integrity reasons deny. Permission events use their own renderer, lifecycle/PostTool unavailability continues, and Cursor fallback allows while malformed-input handling has separate rules.
resolved_source_positions.limits: An availability continuation is not a native evaluated allow and does not establish a receipt. Do not change this behavior to satisfy historical blanket fail-closed prose.

resolved_source_positions.conclusion: The ordinary raw edge returns a validated receipt-bearing Rust result or None. HookWorker records the native receipt before delivery transformation, derives ordinary Watch posture from the same ACKed snapshot and can deliver a warning/allow for a native deny without rewriting the Rust receipt.
resolved_source_positions.limits: Older compatibility functions still have synchronous config reads; the ordinary raw-edge improvement is not a claim that every Python request-time I/O path disappeared.

resolved_source_positions.conclusion: Unset/invalid native mode selects auto. Auto selects the bundled package runtime, ignores arbitrary binary override and does not search PATH. Shadow/force permit explicit development candidates. Off is disablement and yields the current unavailable delivery path, not production Python semantic rollback.
resolved_source_positions.limits: No fresh installed artifact was selected or tested in this review.

resolved_source_positions.conclusion: The source wheel builder accepts the hol-guard pure wheel identity, injects a version/source/rule/digest-bound runtime plus manifest, regenerates RECORD and platform metadata. Desktop staging validates version/target/runtime bytes, and explicit refresh/seal paths account for signing/freeze byte changes.
resolved_source_positions.limits: Packaging machinery and advertised platforms do not prove that a particular final wheel, signed sidecar, installer, update or rollback was exercised. Preserve exact artifact/member/RECORD identity, not installer metadata assumptions.

resolved_source_positions.conclusion: The original contract distinguishes KERNEL, NATIVE_CLIENT, DAEMON_INGRESS and INSTALLED_LAUNCHER distributions. Current source retains separate direct-native and installed-adapter ceilings. PERFORMANCE.md correctly limits its kernel diagnostics and source accounting; neither those diagnostics nor functional route coverage prove installed per-route tail latency.
resolved_source_positions.limits: Keep original five-run/sample/resource requirements and declared targets. Do not pool unlike routes or relabel normalized daemon ingress as installed-launcher latency.
